title: TagDuel explicit lobby-cancellation transaction rollback
scenarios: A SQLite trigger aborts the tag_sessions update to status=cancelled after the host and one invitee have accepted. The original lobby row, consent flags, revision, event set, both locks and player collections must remain unchanged; retry after removing the trigger cancels and releases both locks.

A SQLite trigger aborts deletion of tag_members after the cancelled status update. The transaction must restore the lobby and both locks; retry must cancel once, leave no transition event and release every accepted lock.
invariants: Any accepted human participant may cancel a lobby before duel state exists.
Cancelled status, revision, accepted-member snapshot and all participant-lock deletions are atomic.
Failed cancellation does not leave an orphan session or partial lock release.
Player rows and player_cards remain unchanged; no cards are granted or consumed.
Cancelled lobby has no duel state and no transition-event row.
limits: Tests use temporary SQLite and the real compiled TagStore module.
Fault injection covers SQL trigger aborts, not process termination or filesystem corruption.
No runtime, resolver, catalog manifest, allowlist, persistent database or player data is modified.
This is a lobby-storage regression and certifies no new card behavior.
No live Discord API session is performed.
command: npm run check && npm run build && node --test tests/tagLobbyCancelRollbackAtomicity2v2.test.cjs
